issues.title: Phase 1: AgentKeys MCP server — 7 active tools + 3 schema-only
issues.milestone: M1: First MCP demo + Volcano Ark PoC
issues.body:
## Goal

Ship the AgentKeys MCP server that wraps existing Stage 7+ backend RPCs into MCP-protocol tools. The same MCP server serves both the xiaozhi-server rail (issue #103) and the Volcano Ark rail.

## v1 active tools (7)

- `agentkeys.identity.whoami(actor)` — returns omni, display_name, vendor, scopes
- `agentkeys.memory.get(actor, namespace)` — cap-token verified S3 read; namespace filter
- `agentkeys.memory.put(actor, namespace, content)` — cap-token verified S3 write
- `agentkeys.permission.check(actor, scope, params?)` — **deterministic policy engine, no LLM**
- `agentkeys.cap.mint(actor, op, params, ttl)` — bounded TTL per IAM strategy §3.1
- `agentkeys.cap.revoke(cap_id)` — immediate online, bounded offline
- `agentkeys.audit.append(actor, event)` — emits to two-tier audit (real-time off-chain + 2-min on-chain batch)

## v1 schema-only (3) — return `not_implemented_in_v1`

- `agentkeys.delegation.grant(...)`
- `agentkeys.delegation.revoke(...)`
- `agentkeys.approval.request(...)`

## Stack

- Python (Anthropic `mcp` SDK) — matches xiaozhi-server ecosystem, easier integration
- OR Rust (`mcp-rs`) — matches AgentKeys backend; deferred unless Python proves problematic
- Thin adapter layer over existing broker / signer / worker RPCs; no new backend code

## References

- [`docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md) §4.2 (Phase 1 MCP scope), §3.5 (namespace model)
- [`docs/research/volcano-ark-mcp-integration.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/volcano-ark-mcp-integration.md) §AgentKeys MCP tool inventory
- arch.md §17 (per-data-class isolation), §K-key inventory

## Acceptance

- All 7 active tools respond correctly when called from a stock xiaozhi-server with our MCP server in `mcp_server_settings.json`
- 3 schema-only tools return `not_implemented_in_v1` with clear error
- Per-vendor Bearer token auth + `X-AgentKeys-Actor` header per-actor scoping
- Unit tests + integration test against a mock backend

## Effort

~1 week.

issues.title: Phase 1: Memory namespace model — wire to cap-token + worker filter
issues.milestone: M1: First MCP demo + Volcano Ark PoC
issues.body:
## Goal

Implement the memory namespace model from [`docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md) §3.5. Namespaces are an orthogonal semantic dimension that composes with the 4 structural memory types from [`docs/plan/agentkeys-memory-design.md`](../blob/main/docs/plan/agentkeys-memory-design.md).

## Scope

- Cap-token: add `namespaces_allowed: ["personal", "travel"]` claim
- Wire format: add `namespace: string` field to memory wire envelope (NOT in S3 key derivation — preserves §3.2a)
- Memory worker: filter retrieval results by namespace at request time (deterministic string-set membership)
- v0 default namespaces: `personal`, `family`, `work`, `travel`
- AgentKeys MCP server `memory.get` / `memory.put` accept + enforce namespace

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Path-prefixed namespace layout (preserve current S3 key derivation)
- Per-namespace embedding indexes (use existing global index)
- User-defined custom namespaces (v0 uses the 4 defaults; user-defined → Phase 4)
- `kids` / `device` / `temp` namespaces (Phase 3-4)

## arch.md compatibility check

Verified zero contradictions per IAM strategy §3.5. Compatible with §17.5 (data_class binding), §17 (per-actor PrincipalTag), §K3 epoch rotation, memory-design §1 invariants.

## Acceptance

- A device's cap-token with `namespaces_allowed: ["travel"]` reads only `travel`, denies `personal` / `family` / `work` (returns empty result + audit row)
- Three-act demo Act 1 reads correctly: toy sees Chengdu trip (travel), NOT peanut allergy (personal)

## Effort

~3-4 days (depends on Phase 1 MCP server scaffolding being in place).

issues.title: Phase 1: Two-tier audit wiring (real-time off-chain feed + 2-min on-chain anchor)
issues.milestone: M1: First MCP demo + Volcano Ark PoC
issues.body:
## Goal

Implement the two-tier audit model from [`docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md) §3.2. Real-time off-chain feed for UX; 2-min batched on-chain Merkle root for tamper-evidence.

Follow-up to AuditEnvelope #97.

## Scope

- **Tier 1 (off-chain feed, real-time)**: every authority event (cap mint, permission check, memory read, credential fetch, revocation) → append to off-chain feed + push to parent-control UI via SSE or WebSocket
- **Tier 2 (on-chain anchor, 2-min batch)**: collect events into a Merkle tree; every 2 minutes, write the root on-chain via the existing audit-service worker (tier A from arch.md §15.3)

## Latency commitments

- Tier 1: ~100ms event-to-UI
- Tier 2: ≤2 min event-to-anchor

## arch.md alignment

- Tier 1 = off-chain audit feed (new UX surface)
- Tier 2 = arch.md §15.3 audit-service tier A (Merkle-root anchoring) — already supported as opt-in; flip default for v0 demo

## Acceptance

- Demo Act 2 (deterministic denial): rejection event appears in parent UI instantly; on-chain anchor visible on chain explorer within 2 min
- Demo Act 3 (revocation): revocation event appears in UI instantly + audit chain reflects within 2 min
- Configurable batch cadence (default 2 min, env var `AGENTKEYS_AUDIT_BATCH_SECONDS`)

## Effort

~1 day (mostly wiring; chain anchor logic already exists per audit-service worker).

issues.title: Phase 1: Parent-control web UI (mobile-responsive) for v0 demo
issues.milestone: M1: First MCP demo + Volcano Ark PoC
issues.body:
## Goal

Ship the parent-control web UI required to make the three-act IAM demo legible. Without this, Act 3 (revocation) is invisible and the demo reads as 'smart chatbot.' Per [`docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md) §4.4.

## Scope (mobile-responsive web, NOT native — native is Phase 5)

- Actor list view (devices bound to this user's actor tree)
- Per-actor scope toggles (read/write per namespace, payment cap configuration, time-window limits)
- Revoke buttons (per cap-token, per actor, per scope)
- Real-time audit feed (Tier 1) showing events as they happen
- Link to chain explorer for the Tier 2 batched anchor (no need to embed; just a link with the latest batch hash)

## Stack

- Framework: Next.js or SvelteKit (open to engineer preference; pick one that's familiar)
- Deploy: same demo host (or Vercel for v0 — easier for an early UI)
- Auth: session JWT from broker (K6)

## Out of scope

- Native iOS / Android (Phase 5 = M5)
- Family / work / kids namespace separation UX (Phase 4 = M4)
- Audit replay (Phase 4)

## Acceptance

- Demo Act 3: parent taps 'Revoke FoloToy payment access' → next device attempt fails immediately on online cap-token check
- Real-time audit feed updates within 100ms of an authority event
- Works in iPhone Safari + Chrome Android + desktop browser (mobile-responsive)

## Effort

~3-4 days.

issues.title: Phase 1: Three-act demo runbook + 15-min vendor pitch script
issues.milestone: M1: First MCP demo + Volcano Ark PoC
issues.body:
## Goal

Operator-facing runbook + vendor-facing pitch script so the v0 demo is reproducible and vendor-ready.

## Scope

### `docs/runbooks/demo-three-act-iam.md`

- One-command setup: `bash scripts/setup-demo-iam.sh` (provisions demo MCP server + parent UI + memory mock data + xiaozhi-server config)
- MagicLick 2.5 captive-portal config steps (point at `wss://demo.agentkeys.io/ws`)
- Three-act script: what to say, what the audience sees, troubleshooting per act
- Reset between demos (clear demo state, re-seed memory)

### `docs/pitch/vendor-15min.md`

- 15-minute slide deck outline
- Opening: the vendor's pain (stateless chatbots, no identity, no audit, no portability)
- Three-act live demo (5 minutes)
- The Agent IAM positioning + cross-vendor portability moat
- Pricing structure + how to onboard
- Close: 'what would block you from a pilot in the next 30 days?'

## References

- [`docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md) §4.3 storyboard
- [`docs/research/ai-hardware-companion-wedge.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/ai-hardware-companion-wedge.md) (positioning)

## Acceptance

- A reviewer takes the runbook, runs setup, flashes MagicLick captive-portal config, and within 15 minutes is doing all three acts live
- Demo can be re-run cleanly without manual cleanup between vendor meetings

## Effort

~half day.

issues.title: Phase 1: Volcano Ark MCP marketplace registration (PoC)
issues.milestone: M1: First MCP demo + Volcano Ark PoC
issues.body:
## Goal

Register the AgentKeys MCP server in Volcano Ark's MCP marketplace as a Phase 1 PoC (alongside the xiaozhi rail). Per [`docs/research/volcano-ark-mcp-integration.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/volcano-ark-mcp-integration.md) — VERIFIED FEASIBLE (open international developer signup, no PRC entity required).

## Scope

- Deploy production MCP server at `mcp.agentkeys.io` (TLS, scaling, monitoring)
- Register in [Volcano Ark MCP marketplace](https://mcp.so/server/mcp-server/volcengine)
- Create vendor onboarding token (Bearer token for Doubao agents to authenticate as Volcengine customers)
- Per-actor scoping via `X-AgentKeys-Actor` header
- Verify a Doubao agent (sandbox / test account) can call our tools

## Out of scope (defer to M2)

- Production billing / paid tiers (use free demo tier)
- High-availability multi-region
- Vendor self-service onboarding portal (M2)

## Acceptance

- AgentKeys MCP server listed in Volcano Ark marketplace
- Test Doubao agent successfully invokes `agentkeys.memory.get` from the marketplace listing
- Cross-rail test: same actor's memory read via Doubao MCP returns the same content as via xiaozhi-server

## Effort

~1 week (mostly deployment + marketplace registration paperwork).

issues.title: Phase 2: Vendor onboarding portal (tenant tokens + billing + attributed devices)
issues.milestone: M2: First vendor wedge (incl memory system)
issues.body:
## Goal

Let hardware vendors self-onboard to AgentKeys: create a tenant, issue API tokens, see per-vendor billing, track attributed devices.

## Scope

- Vendor signup flow (email + Stripe/Alipay account binding)
- Tenant token issuance (one Bearer token per vendor for their MCP/SDK clients)
- Per-vendor device registration API: vendor calls `/v1/vendor/devices/register(device_id, user_omni)` → AgentKeys returns `actor_omni` for that device
- Per-vendor billing dashboard (attributed device count, MAU, Pro upgrade revshare)
- Vendor settings: allowed memory namespaces, default cap policies, branding

## Pricing structure (per [`docs/research/ai-hardware-companion-office-hours.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/ai-hardware-companion-office-hours.md))

- $2-3 / active device / month base fee
- 30% lifetime acquirer-of-record revshare on consumer Pro upgrades

## Acceptance

- FoloToy / Ropet / BubblePal can onboard, register devices, see billing
- Pilot vendor signs and integrates within ~1 week

## Effort

~1-2 weeks.

issues.title: Phase 2: Audit dashboard (two-tier visible: real-time feed + chain anchor)
issues.milestone: M2: First vendor wedge (incl memory system)
issues.body:
## Goal

Graduate the v0 parent-UI audit feed (issue: 'Parent-control web UI for v0 demo') to a full audit dashboard suitable for parents + vendor admins + regulator-friendly export.

## Scope

- Filter audit feed by actor, time window, event type, namespace
- Show two tiers side-by-side: real-time off-chain feed + on-chain anchor batches

issues.title: Phase 3: Hermes-MCP server (hermes.execute_task as MCP tool)
issues.milestone: M3: Runtime neutrality
issues.body:
## Goal

Wrap NousResearch Hermes-agent as an MCP server exposing `hermes.execute_task(task, context, constraints)`. Lets the xiaozhi-server LLM (or any MCP client) invoke Hermes for complex multi-step tasks while keeping fast turns on the cheap path.

Per the architectural decision in the session: Agent-as-MCP-tool, NOT LLM-caller-replacement.

## Scope

- Deploy NousResearch Hermes-agent (one instance, can scale later)
- MCP server wrapping Hermes' HTTP gateway
- Tool spec per [`docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md) (Hermes-as-MCP discussion):
  - `hermes.execute_task(task, context: {actor_omni, session_id, memory_namespaces}, constraints: {max_duration_s, max_cost_usd, tools_allowed})` → `{result, steps_taken, cost_usd, audit_trail_id}`
- Hermes uses AgentKeys MCP tools internally (recursive composition: Hermes → AgentKeys tools → S3)

## References

- [`docs/research/xiaozhi-hermes-architecture.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/xiaozhi-hermes-architecture.md)
- [`docs/research/xiaozhi-hermes-risks.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/xiaozhi-hermes-risks.md) (R1-R4 mitigations)

## Acceptance

- A xiaozhi LLM can call `hermes.execute_task` for a complex task ('plan my 3-day Chengdu trip with ¥5000 budget')
- Hermes pulls memory via AgentKeys MCP for context
- End-to-end latency tolerable for non-real-time tasks (30-60s acceptable)

## Effort

~1-2 weeks.

issues.title: Phase 4: Active delegation chains (delegation.grant production)
issues.milestone: M4: Capability + revocation depth
issues.body:
## Goal

Graduate the v1 schema-only `delegation.grant` to production. Parent agent → child agent with scope narrowing + TTL inheritance + revocation cascade + audit chain.

## Scope

- Cap-token format: add `parent_cap_id`, `delegation_chain_depth`, `narrowed_scope`
- Broker: enforce delegated scope ⊆ parent scope (no privilege escalation)
- Revocation cascade: revoking a parent cap revokes all descendants
- Audit chain: every delegated cap-mint emits an audit row with full delegation path
- Maximum delegation depth: 3 (configurable, default 3)

## arch.md update needed

Delegation isn't covered in arch.md yet. Land a new arch.md §X 'Delegation chains' section as part of this issue.

## Acceptance

- A parent agent can delegate a narrowed cap to a child sub-agent
- Revoking the parent revokes all children atomically
- Audit chain reconstructs the full delegation graph for any event

## Effort

~2-3 weeks (includes arch.md design work).

issues.title: Phase 4: Approval workflow (high-risk actions → parent app)
issues.milestone: M4: Capability + revocation depth
issues.body:
## Goal

Graduate the v1 schema-only `approval.request` to production. High-risk actions push to parent-control app for one-tap approval before execution.

## Scope

- Define 'high-risk' policy (configurable per vendor + per actor): payment over X, cred write for sensitive service, memory write to `family` namespace from a non-family-context device, etc.
- Approval request flow: agent calls `agentkeys.approval.request(actor, action, params)` → AgentKeys pushes notification to parent app → parent taps approve/deny → cap-token issued (or refused) → agent proceeds (or fails)
- TTL on pending approvals (default 5 min)
- Audit row for every approval decision

## Acceptance

- Demo: toy requests ¥600 spend (over cap); parent gets push notification; taps approve; spend proceeds
- Same flow with deny: spend fails, audit row shows denial reason

## Effort

~2 weeks.

issues.title: Phase 4: Policy versioning + audit replay
issues.milestone: M4: Capability + revocation depth
issues.body:
## Goal

Let vendors / parents version their policies and replay historical audit events under a different policy to see 'what would have happened.'

## Scope

- Policy versioning: every policy update creates a new version with a timestamp; old versions retained
- Audit replay endpoint: given a time window + a target policy version, replay all events and report what the decision WOULD have been
- Useful for: vendor evaluating a stricter policy before deploying it; parent reviewing 'if I had set this limit yesterday, how many requests would have been denied?'
- Regulator export with policy version stamp on every event

## Acceptance

- Parent / vendor can replay last 7 days of events under a new candidate policy
- Diff report: which events would have changed outcome

## Effort

~1-2 weeks.

issues.title: Phase 7: MCP protocol extensions proposal — IAM-grade auth headers

issues.body:
## Goal

Draft an MCP protocol extension proposal for IAM-grade auth headers: session keys, cap-token forwarding, audit-chain headers. Engage with the MCP working group.

## Scope (after Phase 1-6 land — deferred until traction)

- Spec proposal: `X-AgentKeys-Actor`, `X-AgentKeys-Cap-Token`, `X-AgentKeys-Audit-Chain` headers

## Acceptance

- Draft spec published
- Working group feedback incorporated
- Reference implementation cited by 2+ third-party MCP servers

## Effort

N/A on the engineering side — multi-month standards work.

## Precondition

Do not start until Phase 1-6 land + 10+ vendor deployments + multiple runtime adapter integrations.

issues.title: Phase 7: OAuth-for-Agents specification engagement
issues.milestone: M7: Standards + ecosystem
issues.body:
## Goal

Engage with IETF / W3C on an OAuth-for-Agents specification. Currently OAuth assumes human + app; agent + agent + user + device is a different topology.

## Scope

- Charter proposal to IETF (or whichever working group is most receptive)
- Position paper: how OAuth doesn't fit agent-agent delegation
- Reference implementation cited from AgentKeys deployments

## Acceptance

- Charter accepted (or rejected with feedback informing alternative path)
- AgentKeys' delegation model cited as reference

## Effort

N/A — multi-year standards work.

## Precondition

Same as MCP extensions proposal — defer until vendor traction + multiple deployments.

issues.title: Phase 2: Consumer brand + landing page (name TBD: scoped.ai / leash.ai / bonded.ai)
issues.milestone: M2: First vendor wedge (incl memory system)
issues.body:
## Goal

The consumer face of Agent IAM. Without a consumer brand + landing page, parents have no concept handle for what they're upgrading to in the Pro tier. Per [`docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/agent-iam-strategy.md) §6 Risk 3 (weak consumer face).

## Scope

- Pick brand name: `scoped.ai` / `leash.ai` / `bonded.ai` / another (see [`docs/research/ai-hardware-companion-wedge.md`](../blob/main/docs/research/ai-hardware-companion-wedge.md) §Naming)
- Domain registration + trademark check (international + Chinese-language)
- Single-page landing site: hero ('Your AI memory follows you safely across devices'), 3-act demo video, parent-control app preview, vendor list, pricing
- Privacy / safety / parent-control language — NOT Agent IAM jargon

## Decision dependencies

Name is a leadership call. Trademark search is the cheap gating step.

## Acceptance

- Landing page live with chosen brand
- 'Sign up' CTA → parent-control web UI signup

## Effort

~1 week (name choice is the long pole).
